annotations.description: MstLg Tinker passed priority during combat with Spark Reaper blocked by the 2/5 Carven Caryatid (a brick wall). They could have sacrificed Spark Reaper to its own ability (pay 3 mana) to draw a card and gain 1 life, then in postcombat main cast Bone Picker for just {B} (since a creature died this turn), netting a 3/2 flying deathtouch creature. Instead, Spark Reaper just bounces off the Caryatid accomplishing nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting combat damage resolve with no effect (2/3 vs 2/5, both survive).
annotations.betterLine: Activate Spark Reaper's ability (sacrifice itself, pay {3}) to draw a card and gain 1 life before damage. Then in postcombat main phase, cast Bone Picker for {B} (discounted since a creature died). This converts an ineffective ground creature into a 3/2 flying deathtouch + card advantage.

annotations.description: Timed out and passed the postcombat main phase with 4 untapped Swamps and multiple strong plays available. Most critically, Barter in Blood would have forced the opponent to sacrifice both their creatures (Selfless Savior and Carven Caryatid) while only costing the Spark Reaper. This would have devastated the opponent's board, especially since the Caryatid could become a 4/7 attacker with Warmonger's Chariot. Selfless Savior's ability doesn't help against sacrifice effects.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without casting anything, wasting 4 mana and a critical turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Barter in Blood to force both players to sacrifice two creatures. Opponent loses Selfless Savior and Carven Caryatid; you lose only Spark Reaper (sacrificing one, then having no second creature to sacrifice). This clears the opponent's board and sets up future turns with Bone Picker (cheap after a creature dies) and Liliana's Standard Bearer.

annotations.description: Timed out during postcombat main phase with 4 untapped Swamps and multiple strong plays available. Failed to deploy any creature, wasting an entire turn of development while behind on board.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — passed the turn with 4 mana unused and 5 castable spells in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Bone Picker for {3}{B} to deploy a 3/2 flying deathtouch threat, applying significant evasive pressure. Alternatively, Suspicious Shambler (4/2 with graveyard upside) or Moodmark Painter (giving Spark Reaper menace and +1/+0) would also have been strong plays.

annotations.description: Declined to attack with Selfless Savior when the opponent has no untapped creatures and no untapped lands. This is 1 free damage with zero risk. Selfless Savior can still use its sacrifice ability on subsequent turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Selfless Savior for 1 unblocked damage. The opponent has no blockers available and no mana for tricks.

annotations.description: Player timed out and assigned no blockers. Carven Caryatid (2/5) could have cleanly blocked Spark Reaper (2/3) with no risk, saving 2 damage. Additionally, Crushing Canopy could have been cast to destroy the flying Bone Picker, saving another 3 damage. Instead, the player took the full 5 damage.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — no blockers assigned, took 5 combat damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block Spark Reaper with Carven Caryatid (saves 2 life, Caryatid survives). Optionally also cast Crushing Canopy targeting Bone Picker to destroy it and save 3 more life.

annotations.description: MstLg Tinker passed with Crushing Canopy on the stack targeting Bone Picker, missing the opportunity to sacrifice Bone Picker to Spark Reaper in response (draw a card, gain 1 life, fizzle Canopy), then after combat damage kills Spark Reaper, flash in Liliana's Standard Bearer to draw 2 more cards (2 creatures died this turn). Instead, both creatures die for no value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting Crushing Canopy resolve and destroy Bone Picker with no response.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Spark Reaper sacrificing Bone Picker (3 mana: draw 1, gain 1 life, fizzle Canopy). After combat damage kills Spark Reaper, flash in Liliana's Standard Bearer (2 mana) to draw 2 cards. Net result: 3 extra cards drawn and 1 life gained.

annotations.description: Cast Liliana's Standard Bearer during postcombat main when no creatures died this turn, drawing 0 cards from its ETB trigger. This wastes the card's primary value (flash + card draw after a board wipe or combat deaths). The 3/1 body is fragile and provides less board presence than alternatives.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Liliana's Standard Bearer for 3 mana, getting a 3/1 body with 0 cards drawn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Suspicious Shambler (4/2 for 4 mana) for a bigger, more impactful body with graveyard recursion upside, while holding Liliana's Standard Bearer for a turn where creatures die to get actual card advantage from its ETB. Alternatively, hold up mana and pass, since the 3/1 body doesn't meaningfully change the board state.

annotations.description: Opponent has all lands tapped and no untapped creatures that can block. Selfless Savior could have attacked alongside Carven Caryatid for 1 additional free damage (6 total instead of 5) with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Carven Caryatid (5 damage via Assault Formation)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Selfless Savior and Carven Caryatid for 6 total damage, since the opponent has no untapped blockers and no mana available for instant-speed interaction.

annotations.description: Declined to block Carven Caryatid which deals 5 damage (due to Assault Formation) with available blockers. Pit Keeper (2/1) is a low-value creature that already used its ETB, and blocking with it would prevent 5 damage while also putting another creature card in the graveyard to fuel Moodmark Painter and Ossuary Rats. Taking 5 damage (19→14) to preserve a 2/1 for Barter in Blood sacrifice fodder is a poor trade.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block, taking 5 damage from the Caryatid.
annotations.betterLine: Block with Pit Keeper to prevent 5 damage. Even if planning Barter in Blood next turn, having 2 creatures to sacrifice (Bearer + Reaper) while opponent loses their 2 creatures achieves the same board-clearing effect, and you save 5 life. The extra creature in graveyard also powers up Undergrowth cards.

annotations.description: Blocked Pit Keeper (2/1) with Selfless Savior instead of blocking Liliana's Standard Bearer (3/1). Both blocks result in trades (both creatures have 1 toughness), but blocking the Standard Bearer saves 1 more damage (3 instead of 2) and removes a more threatening creature (3/1 flash vs 2/1).
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Pit Keeper (2/1) with Selfless Savior (1/1), saving 2 damage and trading with a 2/1.
annotations.betterLine: Block Liliana's Standard Bearer (3/1) with Selfless Savior (1/1), saving 3 damage and trading with a more valuable 3/1 creature.

annotations.description: Missed lethal damage. Opponent is at 8 life with all lands tapped and all creatures having summoning sickness (4 Dog tokens are sick). Casting Moodmark Painter (4 creature cards in graveyard = +4/+0 with menace) targeting Spark Reaper would make it a 6/3 with menace. Attacking with both Spark Reaper (6/3 menace) and Moodmark Painter (2/3) deals exactly 8 damage for the kill, with no available blockers on the opponent's side.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase, ending the turn without casting any spells or attacking.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Moodmark Painter targeting Spark Reaper (giving it +4/+0 and menace), then attack with Spark Reaper (6/3) and Moodmark Painter (2/3) for 8 total damage — exactly lethal against the opponent at 8 life with no untapped blockers.

annotations.description: The opponent has no creatures that can block (Ossuary Rats is summoning sick). Both 1/1 Dog tokens could attack for 2 free damage, bringing the opponent from 12 to 10. At 8 life, Gem3P Valley is behind on life and should be taking every opportunity to deal free damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with either Dog token.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both 1/1 Dog tokens for 2 unblockable damage, reducing the opponent to 10 life.

annotations.description: Ossuary Rats (4/3) is blocked by Wall of Vines (0/3) which deals 3 damage via Assault Formation, killing both creatures. Village Rites could sacrifice the doomed Ossuary Rats to draw 2 cards at no real cost - the creature dies in combat regardless. All opponent lands are tapped so there's no risk of a combat trick changing the outcome.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting combat resolve without casting Village Rites
annotations.betterLine: Cast Village Rites sacrificing Ossuary Rats to draw 2 cards for {B}, since the Rats were going to die in combat anyway - pure card advantage for essentially free.

annotations.description: Player timed out on Thriving Heath color choice. The auto-selected color was likely Blue (first option), which produces zero value for this WG deck. Green was the clear correct choice to supplement their green mana for Assault Formation activations ({G} and {2}{G} abilities) and potential future green spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out, likely auto-selecting Blue for Thriving Heath
annotations.betterLine: Choose Green for Thriving Heath to have access to additional green mana for Assault Formation's activated abilities while still producing white mana for the hand full of white spells.

annotations.description: Thriving Heath color choice was made by timeout default, likely resulting in Blue being selected. The deck is WBG with no blue cards, making blue mana completely useless. Green would have been optimal to support Assault Formation's activated abilities ({G} to let defenders attack, {2}{G} for +0/+1), or Black for potential black spells in the deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out on Thriving Heath color choice, likely defaulting to Blue (useless color).
annotations.betterLine: Choose Green to support Assault Formation's activated abilities, or Black if there are black cards in the deck.

annotations.description: With Assault Formation on the battlefield (creatures deal damage equal to toughness), activating its {2}{G} ability to give all creatures +0/+1 would have made both attacking Dog tokens deal 2 damage each (4 total) instead of 1 each (2 total). The opponent is at 10 life, so doubling the combat damage is very significant. The player had exactly enough untapped mana (3 Forests + Plains) to activate this.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed priority without using any abilities during combat, dealing only 2 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Assault Formation's {2}{G} ability to give all creatures +0/+1, making the two Dog tokens deal 4 total damage instead of 2 thanks to toughness-based combat damage.

annotations.description: Moodmark Painter was cast with no other creatures on board, so its ETB can only target itself for a one-turn +6/+0 and menace boost (making it 8/3). The opponent has Grave Bramble and Gargoyle Sentinel available to double-block, potentially killing it. Meanwhile, Revenant would be a 6/6 flyer (6 creature cards in graveyard) that threatens to end the game in 2 attacks against an opponent at 8 life, and the opponent has very limited ways to block flyers (only Gargoyle Sentinel with 3 mana activation, and they have only 1 untapped land).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Moodmark Painter, a 2/3 with a one-turn ETB buff targeting itself
annotations.betterLine: Cast Revenant as a 6/6 flyer that attacks over most blockers and threatens lethal in 2 turns against an opponent at 8 life with minimal flying defense

annotations.description: Moodmark Painter's Undergrowth trigger was auto-targeted to an opponent's Dog Token due to timeout/passing, giving the opponent's 1/1 Dog menace and +7/+0 (making it 8/1). This helps the opponent enormously while wasting the powerful ETB trigger. The opponent is at 8 life and MstLg Tinker has 7 creatures in graveyard.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed/timed out, causing the trigger to auto-target an opponent's Dog Token, giving it menace and +7/+0.
annotations.betterLine: Target Moodmark Painter itself, making it a 9/3 with menace. This threatens lethal damage against the 8-life opponent, as a 9/3 menace creature is extremely difficult to profitably block.

annotations.description: With Assault Formation on the battlefield (creatures deal damage equal to toughness) and 1 untapped Forest, Gem3P Valley could activate Assault Formation's {G} ability to let Grave Bramble (3/4 defender) attack this turn, dealing 4 damage to the opponent at 10 life. The opponent's only creature (Moodmark Painter) is summoning sick and can't block. This is 4 free damage that brings the opponent to 6 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Assault Formation, missing the attack with Grave Bramble.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Assault Formation targeting Grave Bramble for {G}, then attack with Grave Bramble for 4 damage, putting the opponent to 6 life.

annotations.description: Player timed out during precombat main phase with 5 mana available, multiple castable spells (Pacifism, Cathar's Companion, Feat of Resistance), and a strong Assault Formation board that could pressure the opponent at 10 life. Moodmark Painter is extremely dangerous with 10 creatures in opponent's graveyard (potential +10/+0 and menace). Missing the entire turn's actions at 8 life in a close game is devastating.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out - no action taken, effectively passing the entire turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Pacifism on Moodmark Painter to neutralize its massive Undergrowth threat, then cast Cathar's Companion as an additional body. Use Assault Formation to enable Grave Bramble to attack, pressuring opponent's 10 life total.

annotations.description: Opponent has no untapped creatures that can block (Moodmark Painter is summoning sick). Both Dog Tokens could attack for 2 free damage with zero risk. Additionally, Gargoyle Sentinel could be activated for 3 mana to attack for 3 more (5 total damage, bringing opponent from 10 to 5). Missing 2-5 free damage against an opponent at 10 life while you're at 8 life is a significant mistake in a race situation.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed combat without declaring any attackers, dealing 0 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Dog Tokens for 2 guaranteed damage. Ideally also activate Gargoyle Sentinel (3 mana) to attack for 3 flying damage, dealing 5 total and putting opponent to 5 life. Keep remaining mana open for Feat of Resistance or Assault Formation pump if needed.

annotations.description: Opponent is casting Pacifism on Moodmark Painter, which will render it useless. Village Rites could sacrifice the Painter in response, fizzling Pacifism and drawing 2 cards. This also increases graveyard creature count to 11, powering up the Revenant in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing Pacifism to resolve on Moodmark Painter
annotations.betterLine: Cast Village Rites sacrificing Moodmark Painter in response to Pacifism. This fizzles Pacifism (wasting opponent's card and mana), draws 2 cards, and grows the graveyard for Revenant.

annotations.description: MstLg Tinker has a Thriving Moor in hand and 1 land drop remaining in their postcombat main phase, but passes priority without playing it. This wastes a free land drop that would give them an additional mana source next turn. With cards like Caged Zombie (3 mana) and Suspicious Shambler (4 mana) in hand, plus the potential to activate Malefic Scythe's equip cost, having an extra land in play is meaningful. There's no reason not to play a tapped land in the postcombat main phase.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing Thriving Moor, ending the turn with an unused land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Moor (choosing an appropriate color) to have 8 mana sources available next turn, enabling more flexibility to cast multiple spells or activate abilities.

annotations.description: Blocked a 1/1 Dog Token instead of the 5/6 Grave Bramble (dealing 6 damage via Assault Formation). Blocking the Dog prevents only 1 damage, while blocking Grave Bramble prevents 6 damage (no trample). This results in taking 7 damage (down to 3 life) instead of 2 damage (down to 8 life), putting MstLg Tinker in a critically dangerous position.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked a 1/1 Dog Token with the Soldier Token, preventing only 1 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block Grave Bramble with the Soldier Token to prevent 6 damage, going to 8 life instead of 3 life.

annotations.description: At 2 life with the opponent at 8, MstLg Tinker is in a desperate racing situation. All of the opponent's creatures are tapped, so only Gargoyle Sentinel (with defender) can block. Sending both Eternal Taskmaster and Soldier Token would force the opponent to let at least one through, dealing 1 extra damage. The 1/1 Soldier Token's defensive value is marginal when the opponent has creatures like Grave Bramble 5/6 that will untap next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Eternal Taskmaster, holding back the Soldier Token
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Eternal Taskmaster and Soldier Token to maximize damage through the single available blocker (Gargoyle Sentinel), dealing at least 1 extra damage to the opponent at 8 life

annotations.description: Gargoyle Sentinel (3/3) could block and kill Eternal Taskmaster (2/3) while surviving. The opponent has only 1 untapped Swamp, making combat tricks extremely unlikely. Not blocking lets the Taskmaster survive to attack again and potentially recur creatures from the graveyard. Taking 2 damage (8→6) is unnecessary when you can kill the attacker for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block Eternal Taskmaster with Gargoyle Sentinel, taking 2 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block Eternal Taskmaster with Gargoyle Sentinel to kill it while the Gargoyle survives at 3/1. This removes a recursive threat for free.

annotations.description: Activated Fetid Imp's deathtouch ability during own combat phase, but Fetid Imp has summoning sickness and cannot attack or block this turn. The deathtouch wears off at end of turn, so it provides zero benefit. This wastes the last untapped black mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Fetid Imp to give it deathtouch until end of turn during own combat phase
annotations.betterLine: Do not activate Fetid Imp's ability since it has summoning sickness and can't participate in combat. Keep the mana open in case of any instant-speed needs or simply save it.

annotations.description: Player timed out in precombat main phase with opponent at 2 life and clear lethal on board. Should have cast Cathar's Companion for additional insurance and/or prepared for combat. The timeout risks cascading through combat phases, potentially missing lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out (no response), passing precombat main without casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Cathar's Companion for an additional attacker, then move to combat. Attack with both Dog tokens and activate Gargoyle Sentinel ({3} to lose defender and gain flying). Opponent only has a 1/1 Soldier token to block, so at minimum 4+ damage gets through against 2 life for lethal.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 2 life. Gem3P Valley has two 1/1 Dog tokens, a 3/3 Gargoyle Sentinel, and a 5/6 Grave Bramble (with Assault Formation letting creatures deal damage equal to toughness, and Warmonger's Chariot or Assault Formation's ability allowing defenders to attack). The opponent has very limited blockers: Eternal Taskmaster is tapped, Caged Zombie and Fetid Imp are summoning sick, and there's only a 1/1 Soldier token untapped. Attacking with everything would deal far more than 2 damage even through a single block — this is lethal on board. The player timed out and failed to declare any attackers, completely missing a guaranteed lethal attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out (no response) and declared no attackers, passing through combat without attacking.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (two Dog tokens, Gargoyle Sentinel, and Grave Bramble). The opponent can only block one attacker with the 1/1 Soldier token. Even blocking one Dog token, the remaining attackers deal at least 2 damage (another Dog token alone), which is lethal against the opponent's 2 life. Use Assault Formation's {G} ability to let Grave Bramble attack if needed.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 2 life with only a 1/1 Soldier Token as an available blocker (all other creatures are either tapped or summoning sick). Gargoyle Sentinel can be activated for {3} to gain flying and attack for 3 unblockable damage, which is lethal. Even just attacking with the two Dog Tokens forces 1 damage through. Multiple lines result in lethal damage this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers, missing lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Gargoyle Sentinel for {3} to lose defender and gain flying, then attack with Gargoyle Sentinel (3 flying damage, unblockable) for lethal. Alternatively, attack with all available creatures to overwhelm the single 1/1 blocker.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing 11 damage from attackers (Grave Bramble dealing 6 via Assault Formation, Gargoyle Sentinel dealing 3 with flying, two Dog Tokens dealing 1 each), MstLg Tinker declared no blockers, which is immediately lethal. With optimal blocking - Fetid Imp (with deathtouch activation) blocking Gargoyle Sentinel, Caged Zombie blocking Grave Bramble, and Soldier Token blocking one Dog Token - only 1 damage would get through, leaving them alive at 1 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Declared no blockers, taking 11 damage at 2 life (lethal).
annotations.betterLine: Block Gargoyle Sentinel with Fetid Imp (activate deathtouch for B), block Grave Bramble with Caged Zombie, block one Dog Token with Soldier Token. This blocks 10 of 11 damage, surviving at 1 life.
